# ZMem

ZMem is agent-native local memory for AI agents.

It lets agents request approved memory, propose new memory, explain what memory shaped an action, and hand off governed memory state to another agent.

## Product Positioning

ZMem is not just a vector store or recall provider. It is a local-first memory layer for agents that need continuity, inspection, control, and proof.

Core loop:

- Ask: an agent calls `memory.inject` before a task.
- Learn: an agent calls `memory.propose` after a task.
- Review: a human or configured authority promotes, rejects, quarantines, or revokes proposed memory.
- Act: the agent uses only approved injected memory.
- Explain: the agent calls `memory.why` to show which memory influenced an action.
- Handoff: ZMem exports snapshots, restore guides, prompts, and receipt bundles so another agent can continue.

## What Agents Get

- Durable local memory across sessions and tools.
- Approved memory context scoped to the current task.
- A review-safe way to write new memory.
- Receipts for memory-backed actions.
- Handoff artifacts for Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenClaw, Hermes, and generic MCP clients.
- Chat-to-chat continuity through shared local stores, proposed checkpoints, and verified handoff/restore packages.

## What Humans Get

- Local SQLite storage.
- Typed, searchable memories.
- Source, scope, trust, authority, labels, lifecycle, lineage, and revocation.
- Dashboard inspection.
- Review queue for proposed or risky memories.
- Merkle roots, action receipts, why reports, snapshots, and return packets.

## Agent Usage

Before a task:

```text
memory.inject
```

Use the returned `memories` as durable context. Treat returned `withheld` memories as unavailable and non-authoritative.

After a task:

```text
memory.propose
```

Use this for durable facts, procedures, preferences, failed attempts, recovery notes, and policy candidates.

When memory shaped an action:

```text
memory.why
```

Use the returned action id to explain what was injected, what was withheld, and which policy or memory root applied.

## MCP Tools

```text
memory.remember
memory.propose
memory.search
memory.inject
memory.inspect
memory.queue
memory.promote
memory.reject
memory.lineage
memory.revoke
memory.forget
memory.why
memory.verify
memory.external_search
memory.external_import
memory.snapshot
memory.restore
```

## CLI

```bash
zmem status --summary-only
zmem ui
zmem agent install codex
zmem agent install claude-code
zmem agent install cursor --summary-only
zmem agent pack --summary-only
zmem handoff --summary-only
zmem verify <action-id>
```

## Chat-To-Chat Continuity

Same workspace:

```bash
zmem inject "continue the task" --agent codex --scope project --risk medium
```

Pasted summary from another chat:

```bash
zmem propose "Cross-chat checkpoint: ..." --type episodic --scope project --source agent --label cross-chat-checkpoint
zmem queue --scope project --status quarantined
zmem promote <memory-id>
```

Different workspace or machine:

```bash
zmem handoff --summary-only
zmem --db .zerker/imported.sqlite restore --handoff-dir .zerker/handoff
```

## Rules For Agents

- Do not treat prior chat memory as durable unless ZMem injects it.
- Do not promote your own proposed memories.
- Do not use withheld, revoked, quarantined, or low-authority memory as context.
- Keep the `action_id` when memory influenced an action.
- Use `memory.why` when asked why memory mattered.
- Use handoff artifacts before transferring work to another agent.
- Treat pasted chat summaries as proposed memory until reviewed.
